title: AlgaMetrix: open-source techno-economic analysis and life-cycle assessment for microalgae and aquatic protist biomass
description:
AlgaMetrix is a free and open-source tool for the techno-economic analysis (TEA) and life-cycle assessment (LCA) of microalgal, cyanobacterial and thraustochytrid (aquatic protist) biomass.

Both analyses are derived from a single shared mass and energy balance, so the economic and the environmental results always describe the same process rather than two independently parameterised models. From a user-defined production scenario it computes the process inventory, a SuperPro-style capital structure, the minimum biomass production cost, a discounted cash-flow profitability model (NPV, IRR, break-even selling price), cradle-to-gate impacts (GWP, cumulative energy demand, water, land, eutrophication, acidification), downstream extraction with cost and impact allocation across co-products, one-dimensional sensitivity sweeps and Monte-Carlo uncertainty propagation.

It ships as a PySide6 desktop application built on a UI-agnostic Python engine that can equally be driven from a script or a notebook. Every organism, cultivation system, price and characterization factor lives in editable, citable YAML files under data/: there are no hidden numbers. Cultivation systems include open raceway ponds, tubular, flat-panel and bubble-column photobioreactors, thin-layer cascades, a bicarbonate-fed Spirulina raceway, and a stirred-tank heterotrophic fermenter.

Note on defaults: the bundled parameter values are literature-typical placeholders that make the tool run out of the box. They are not validated for any specific plant and should be replaced with the user's own data.
